narratives.name: AI Platform Domain Context and Rationale
narratives.description: Why structured AI platform positioning across five tactic areas enables credible technology-specific conversations.

narrativeContexts.context: Enterprise AI adoption spans multiple distinct scenarios -- from deploying inference models at scale through sovereign AI compliance to autonomous agentic workflows -- each requiring specialized infrastructure knowledge and competitive positioning that generic AI messaging cannot provide.

The AI Platform Domain structures positioning across five tactic areas, each addressing a specific AI customer challenge pattern. Sellers can assess customer AI maturity, design platform architectures, engage with tactic-level conversations, validate technology fit, and advance decisions using AI-domain-specific credentials, customer wins, and competitive intelligence.

Structured AI platform positioning enables sellers to engage credibly across the full AI landscape, from basic inference deployment through cutting-edge agentic AI, while maintaining consistent competitive differentiation against cloud AI services and proprietary platforms.

narratives.name: AI Platform TDP Practice Intent
narratives.description: The end-to-end narrative of AI platform technology positioning from strategy assessment through tactic execution to decision conversion.

narrativeContexts.context: Enterprise organizations pursuing AI transformation face a fragmented technology landscape where cloud-native AI services, proprietary platforms, and open-source frameworks compete for adoption. Red Hat's AI Platform TDP equips sellers with positioning across five distinct AI scenarios -- inference at scale, sovereign AI, production AI, agentic AI, and NVIDIA partnership solutions -- each addressing a specific customer challenge pattern in the rapidly evolving AI infrastructure market.

The TDP's value is validated through its breadth of tactic coverage across the full AI lifecycle. Sellers can position Red Hat for customers deploying their first inference workloads, customers requiring sovereign AI within regulatory constraints, organizations scaling AI into production with MLOps governance, enterprises exploring autonomous agentic AI workflows, and joint Red Hat-NVIDIA AI Factory infrastructure. Each tactic provides audience-segmented content with competitive positioning against cloud AI services and proprietary AI platforms.

AI Platform TDP activation provides sellers with comprehensive AI domain credentials, customer reference stories, and structured What to Say/Share/Show content across all five tactic areas. The NVIDIA co-sell tactic provides unique partnership-specific content with joint solution architectures, enabling sellers to leverage the NVIDIA relationship for infrastructure-level AI deals.

Field execution combines tactic-level AI customer conversations with TDP-level technology depth to create multi-dimensional engagements. Sellers can navigate from a customer's specific AI challenge (via tactic) to Red Hat's broader AI platform credentials (via TDP) and back, using bidirectional framework navigation to adapt to each customer's AI maturity and decision context.

AI platform technology decisions convert when sellers demonstrate infrastructure-level value beyond any single AI framework. Proof activities validate model serving performance, GPU utilization efficiency, MLOps lifecycle management, and governance compliance against the customer's specific AI workload requirements.

Continuous optimization driven by AI market evolution sustains TDP relevance. Tactic content is refreshed as new AI paradigms emerge (agentic AI being the latest), competitive positioning adapts as cloud providers enhance their AI services, and NVIDIA partnership content evolves with new GPU generations and joint solutions.

narratives.name: Inference at Scale Tactic Context and Rationale
narratives.description: Why challenge-focused inference conversation converts infrastructure interest into platform opportunities.

narrativeContexts.context: Organizations deploying AI inference workloads face infrastructure complexity around GPU scheduling, model serving latency, and cost management that cloud-native services address with convenience but at the expense of flexibility, portability, and cost transparency.

The Inference at Scale tactic equips sellers with challenge-focused conversation content that frames inference infrastructure as a platform engineering problem, positioning Red Hat's model serving capabilities as an open, portable alternative to proprietary cloud inference endpoints.

Sellers who execute the inference tactic effectively convert AI infrastructure conversations from feature comparisons into platform strategy discussions, expanding deal scope from single-model deployment to enterprise-wide inference infrastructure.

narratives.name: Sovereign AI Tactic Context and Rationale
narratives.description: Why sovereignty-focused AI positioning creates differentiated opportunities in regulated markets.

narrativeContexts.context: Organizations in regulated industries and sovereignty-sensitive geographies must deploy AI capabilities while maintaining full control over model provenance, training data residency, and inference infrastructure -- requirements that cloud-native AI services cannot guarantee due to shared infrastructure and opaque model governance.

The Sovereign AI tactic equips sellers with challenge-focused content that frames AI sovereignty as a compliance and control imperative, positioning Red Hat's on-premise and sovereign cloud AI platform as the open-source foundation for AI deployments that must meet stringent regulatory and geopolitical requirements.

Sellers executing the sovereign AI tactic create differentiated positioning in regulated markets where proprietary and cloud AI services face structural limitations, expanding deal scope by connecting AI infrastructure to broader digital sovereignty transformation initiatives.

Sellers executing the production AI tactic convert AI experimentation conversations into enterprise MLOps platform opportunities, helping customers bridge the gap between proof-of-concept AI and production-scale model management with governance and compliance built in.

narratives.name: AI Platform Competitive Position Context and Rationale
narratives.description: Why multi-category AI competitive intelligence is essential for platform positioning.

narrativeContexts.context: AI platform decisions involve evaluation of cloud-native AI services (AWS SageMaker, Azure ML, Google Vertex AI), proprietary AI platforms (Databricks, Dataiku), and open-source AI infrastructure alternatives. Each competitive category has genuine strengths -- cloud services offer convenience and elastic scaling, proprietary platforms offer integrated data-to-model workflows, and the competitive dynamics evolve rapidly as new AI capabilities emerge.

Cloud AI services provide managed convenience and rapid prototyping but create data gravity, model portability challenges, and unpredictable GPU consumption costs at scale. Proprietary AI platforms offer integrated workflows but risk vendor lock-in and limit model interoperability. Each alternative serves specific AI use cases well while creating long-term strategic constraints.

Red Hat's AI platform provides a structural competitive advantage through open-source model governance (transparency and portability), hybrid deployment flexibility (cloud, on-premise, sovereign), NVIDIA partnership validation (enterprise-grade GPU infrastructure), and consistent platform experience across AI scenarios. The five-tactic approach ensures competitive positioning adapts to each customer's specific AI challenge context rather than relying on a single competitive pitch.

narratives.name: Assess AI Platform Landscape Technique
narratives.description: How to evaluate customer AI maturity and select the most relevant tactic for engagement.

narrativeContexts.context: AI platform positioning requires understanding the customer's AI maturity before selecting which of the five available tactics is most relevant, since premature tactic selection risks misaligning the conversation with the customer's actual AI journey stage.

Begin by evaluating the customer's AI maturity across a five-stage spectrum (experimentation through enterprise), cataloguing their AI use cases, and assessing their infrastructure readiness including GPU availability and data architecture. Map findings to the five AI platform tactics to identify the best entry point.

A thorough AI landscape assessment ensures that tactic selection matches the customer's actual AI maturity and priorities, increasing the relevance and conversion potential of subsequent tactic-level conversations.

narratives.name: Design AI Platform Architecture Technique
narratives.description: How to design an AI platform architecture that demonstrates technical depth and competitive differentiation.

narrativeContexts.context: AI platform architecture decisions are complex, spanning deployment models (on-premise, cloud, hybrid, sovereign), model serving patterns, MLOps pipelines, GPU management, and governance -- and sellers must design solutions that address all these dimensions while differentiating from cloud-native and proprietary alternatives.

Work with the customer's technical team to design an AI platform topology that matches their deployment preferences and compliance requirements. Specify model serving architecture with clear performance requirements, design MLOps pipelines that span the full model lifecycle, and plan GPU resource management with cost optimization.

A well-designed AI platform architecture demonstrates technical depth and creates a differentiated solution proposal that addresses the customer's specific AI infrastructure requirements rather than offering a generic platform pitch.

narratives.name: Execute AI Platform Tactic Conversation Technique
narratives.description: How to deliver AI-specific tactic conversations that establish relevance through customer challenge framing.

narrativeContexts.context: AI customer conversations require tactic-specific depth -- an inference scaling conversation differs fundamentally from a sovereign AI compliance conversation or an agentic AI infrastructure conversation -- and generic AI messaging fails to establish relevance for the customer's specific challenge.

Execute the selected AI tactic's conversation guide, leading with the customer's challenge framing before positioning Red Hat's capabilities. Deliver audience-segmented content, share relevant evidence and demonstrations, and navigate bidirectionally to other AI tactics or the broader AI Platform TDP when the conversation reveals additional technology concerns.

Tactic-level execution converts AI infrastructure interest into qualified opportunities by establishing relevance through customer challenge framing, demonstrating technical depth through AI-specific evidence, and tracking engagement to inform follow-up strategy.

narratives.name: Position AI Platform Competitively Technique
narratives.description: How to address multiple competitive categories in AI platform evaluations with evidence-based differentiation.

narrativeContexts.context: AI platform competitive positioning must address multiple competitive categories simultaneously -- cloud AI services (convenience, elastic scaling), proprietary platforms (integrated workflows, managed experience), and open-source alternatives (cost, flexibility) -- with each customer evaluation context emphasizing different competitive dimensions.

Cloud AI services offer managed convenience and rapid prototyping but create data gravity and model portability challenges. Proprietary platforms offer integrated workflows but risk vendor lock-in. Open-source framework-only approaches offer flexibility but lack enterprise governance and support.

Red Hat's AI platform combines open-source transparency with enterprise support, hybrid deployment flexibility with consistent platform experience, and NVIDIA partnership validation with GPU infrastructure expertise. The five-tactic approach ensures competitive positioning adapts to each customer's specific AI challenge context.

narratives.name: Validate AI Platform Technology Fit Technique
narratives.description: How to design AI-specific validation activities that prove infrastructure-level capabilities.

narrativeContexts.context: AI platform technology validation is uniquely demanding because it must demonstrate performance across multiple dimensions -- model serving latency, GPU utilization efficiency, MLOps pipeline robustness, and governance compliance -- each with customer-specific benchmarks that cannot be addressed through generic demonstrations.

Design AI-specific validation activities using each TDP tactic's What to Show content as a foundation. For inference workloads, validate model serving performance and GPU scheduling. For production AI, demonstrate MLOps lifecycle management. For sovereign AI, prove governance compliance. Structure validation with clear success criteria aligned to the customer's specific AI decision criteria.

Successful AI platform validation converts technical interest into committed decisions by proving infrastructure-level capabilities that cloud AI services and proprietary platforms cannot match for the customer's specific deployment model, scale, and compliance requirements.

narratives.name: Advance AI Platform Decision Technique
narratives.description: How to convert validated AI platform evaluation into committed procurement with expansion pathways.

narrativeContexts.context: Converting a validated AI platform evaluation into a committed procurement decision requires bridging the gap between technical proof and commercial commitment, including infrastructure sizing, partner ecosystem alignment, and expansion roadmap definition.

Work with the customer to complete GPU and infrastructure sizing based on validated workload requirements. Align NVIDIA and ISV partnerships as applicable. Establish an expansion roadmap covering additional AI models, use cases, and deployment environments. Ensure win attribution to the AI Platform TDP for performance measurement.

A well-managed AI platform decision process converts validated technical evaluations into committed deals with clear expansion pathways, maximizing deal value through infrastructure-level scope rather than single-workload purchases.

narratives.name: Gather AI Platform Competitive Intelligence Technique
narratives.description: How to establish systematic AI competitive intelligence that keeps tactic positioning current.

narrativeContexts.context: The AI platform competitive landscape evolves rapidly as cloud providers continuously enhance their AI services, new proprietary platforms emerge, and open-source AI frameworks proliferate, requiring continuous intelligence gathering to maintain current and credible competitive positioning.

Establish systematic AI competitive intelligence collection covering cloud AI services (feature releases, pricing changes, analyst evaluations), proprietary platforms (market positioning, customer acquisition), and GPU infrastructure partnerships. Integrate win/loss data from AI-related opportunities to validate competitive claims with field evidence.

Continuously updated AI competitive intelligence ensures that tactic-level competitive positioning reflects the latest market dynamics, enabling sellers to address competitive objections with current evidence rather than stale comparison data.
